COMT inhibitors (entacapone, tolcapone) pharmacologically block this step, raising plasma catecholamines including epinephrine.

causal:influence:gip:positive:plasma_ins.evidence: Nauck & Meier 2021 Diabetes Obes Metab (GIP insulinotropic action) | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-097 (17.10: The Endocrine Pancreas): GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide) is the initial trigger for insulin production and secretion by beta cells following food ingestion; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-098 (17.11: Organs with Secondary Endocrine Functions): 'Glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) — Stimulate beta cells of the pancreas to release insulin'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-135 (23.6: The Small and Large Intestines): 'K cells [secrete] the hormone glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide, which stimulates the release of insulin'
causal:influence:gip:positive:plasma_ins.mechanism: GIP binds beta-cell GIPR, potentiating glucose-dependent insulin secretion

causal:influence:glp1:negative:gastric_e.evidence: "GLP1 is an incretin hormone produced in the gut that has been shown to boost glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon secretion, delay gastric emptying" — Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 36, p 1434  ||  "In addition to enhancing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, slowing gastric emptying, and inhibiting gastric acid secretion, these compounds reduce food intake" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 39, p 1565
causal:influence:glp1:negative:gastric_e.mechanism: GLP-1 → vagal/enteric nerve GLP-1R signaling disposition → slowed gastric motility

causal:influence:glutathione_synthetase_.evidence: OMMBID glutathione synthetase deficiency — massive 5-oxoprolinuria (pyroglutamic aciduria)
causal:influence:glutathione_synthetase_.mechanism: GSS deficiency disinhibits gamma-GCS (loss of glutathione feedback), overproducing gamma-glutamylcysteine which is converted to 5-oxoproline, raising 5-oxoproline

causal:influence:glycine_cleavage_enzyme.evidence: Harrison's / OMMBID nonketotic hyperglycinemia (glycine encephalopathy, GLDC/AMT) — HYPERglycinemia
causal:influence:glycine_cleavage_enzyme.mechanism: the glycine cleavage system (GCS) is the principal route of glycine catabolism; reduced GCS activity (nonketotic hyperglycinemia) causes glycine to accumulate

causal:influence:gnrh:positive:gonadotro.evidence: "FSH secretion ... changes more slowly over a period of many hours in response to longer-term changes in GnRH." — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 80, p. 1007-1008
causal:influence:gnrh:positive:gonadotro.mechanism: GnRH stimulates gonadotroph FSH secretion (responds to longer-term GnRH changes rather than each pulse)

causal:influence:hal_activity:negative:c.evidence: Histidinemia (HAL/histidase deficiency, OMIM 235800) — elevated plasma and CSF histidine; Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (histidinemia: histidine elevated in plasma, urine, and CSF); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (histidine catabolism: HAL deaminates histidine to urocanate). | intervention: do(HAL LoF) — histidinemia
causal:influence:hal_activity:negative:c.mechanism: Histidine ammonia-lyase (HAL/histidase) converts histidine to urocanate + ammonia; HAL deficiency (histidinemia) blocks histidine catabolism, causing histidine to accumulate in plasma and CSF.

causal:influence:heart_rate:negative:end.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-109 (19.5: Cardiac Physiology): 'as the HR rises, there is less time spent in diastole and consequently less time for the ventricles to fill with blood … SV gradually decreases due to decreased filling time.'
causal:influence:heart_rate:negative:end.mechanism: Higher heart rate shortens diastolic filling time, reducing ventricular filling and EDV (preload).

causal:influence:hepatic_bilirubin_conju.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 'Jaundice' (impaired conjugation -> unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia; Gilbert OMIM 143500, Crigler-Najjar OMIM 218800); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology
causal:influence:hepatic_bilirubin_conju.mechanism: conjugation consumes intracellular unconjugated bilirubin; higher conjugation flux lowers the unconjugated pool that equilibrates with plasma (UGT1A1 LoF therefore RAISES plasma unconjugated bilirubin)

causal:influence:hgprt_activity:negative.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (salvage vs catabolic fate of hypoxanthine/guanine); Lesch-Nyhan HPRT1 OMIM 300322 (HGPRT loss -> uric acid overproduction); Harrison's hyperuricemia/gout
causal:influence:hgprt_activity:negative.mechanism: hypoxanthine/guanine not salvaged by HGPRT are diverted into the xanthine-oxidase catabolic pathway to uric acid; loss of HGPRT (Lesch-Nyhan) routes more substrate to urate, so HGPRT activity is inversely related to urate production

causal:influence:hmg_coa_lyase_activity:.evidence: HMG-CoA lyase deficiency (HMGCLD; OMIM 246450): hypoketotic hypoglycemia is the hallmark clinical presentation — patients have low plasma ketone bodies despite fasting and elevated FFA because HMG-CoA lyase is required for hepatic ketogenesis (OMIM 246450; PMC9136170; Frontiers in Genetics 2022 doi:10.3389/fgene.2022.880464). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry ch. 17 (ketogenesis pathway; HMG-CoA lyase as the ketone-forming step). | intervention: do(HMGCL LoF) -> HMG-CoA lyase activity falls -> ketone body synthesis blocked -> plasma ketone bodies fall (hypoketotic)
causal:influence:hmg_coa_lyase_activity:.mechanism: HMG-CoA lyase is the enzyme that produces acetoacetate (and thereby all ketone bodies) from HMG-CoA in the liver. Deficiency blocks ketone body production, causing hypoketotic hypoglycemia during catabolic crises: despite elevated free fatty acids (the usual ketogenic substrate), ketone bodies cannot be formed. More lyase activity generates more acetoacetate and ketone bodies.

causal:influence:hypothalamic_gabaergic_.evidence: Antisense oligodeoxynucleotides for GAD67 and GAD65 mRNAs infused into the stalk median eminence of prepubertal monkeys induced a striking increase in GnRH release, whereas nonsense d-oligos did not. Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26  ||  chronic, repetitive administration of bicuculline, a GABA inhibitor, into the base of the third ventricle of a prepubertal monkey caused premature menarche and the onset of the first ovulation. Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26
causal:influence:hypothalamic_gabaergic_.mechanism: GABA inhibits GnRH pulse generator; antisense oligodeoxynucleotides to GAD67/65 (enzymes synthesizing GABA) increase GnRH release; bicuculline (GABA antagonist) causes premature menarche

causal:influence:il1beta:positive:crh.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology (cytokine activation of the HPA axis, IL-1 -> CRH); Janeway's Immunobiology
causal:influence:il1beta:positive:crh.mechanism: IL-1beta acts on hypothalamic paraventricular neurons to stimulate CRH release (immune-to-HPA signaling)

causal:influence:il6:positive:plasma_ca1.evidence: Mechanical stretch and inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-8) directly upregulate MUC16/CA125 expression and shedding from mesothelial cells; serum CA125 correlates positively with serum IL-6/TNF-alpha in heart failure. PMID:22743023 (Kosar/Huang et al., 'New mechanism of elevated CA125 in heart failure: the mechanical stress and inflammatory stimuli initiate CA125 synthesis', Med Hypotheses 2012) — verified real.
causal:influence:il6:positive:plasma_ca1.mechanism: CA125 (MUC16) is produced by mesothelial cells lining the serous cavities. In non-malignant states inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1beta) via NF-kB induce MUC16 synthesis and ectodomain shedding from mesothelial cells, raising serum CA125. do(IL-6 up) -> mesothelial MUC16 synthesis/shedding up -> plasma CA125 up.

causal:influence:kynu_activity:positive:.evidence: Shi H et al. NEJM 2017 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1616361) — biallelic KYNU LoF is one of three causes of congenital NAD deficiency disorder (CNDD); 'affected patients had biallelic pathogenic variants in KYNU, HAAO, or NADSYN1, all essential genes of NAD de novo synthesis'. GeneReviews NBK593504 (CNDD). OMIM 236800 (hydroxykynureninuria / KYNU deficiency). Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (kynurenine pathway to NAD+; KYNU step is obligate for flux from 3-HK to 3-HAA). | intervention: do(KYNU biallelic LoF) = hydroxykynureninuria / CNDD: 3-HK not cleaved → de novo NAD+ pathway blocked → cellular NADH reduced | intervention: do(KYNU biallelic LoF) — hydroxykynureninuria / congenital NAD deficiency disorder, OMIM 236800 / Shi NEJM 2017
causal:influence:kynu_activity:positive:.mechanism: Kynureninase (KYNU, gene KYNU) catalyses the PLP-dependent hydrolysis of 3-hydroxykynurenine to 3-hydroxyanthranilate, a step required for de novo NAD+ biosynthesis from tryptophan via the kynurenine pathway. KYNU LoF blocks flux to 3-hydroxyanthranilate and all downstream de novo NAD+ precursors (quinolinate via HAAO → NaMN via QPRT → NAD+), reducing the total cellular NAD+ pool and hence cellular NADH. Sign: more KYNU activity → more 3-hydroxyanthranilate → more quinolinate → more de novo NAD+/NADH (do(KYNU biallelic LoF) = cellular NAD+/NADH falls). [Note: kynu_activity (PR:000009598) and kynureninase_activity (PR:Q16719) are two model nodes for the same KYNU enzyme encoded in separate fragments; the bridge mechanism is identical.]

causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism; OMIM 238600 (LPL deficiency); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology, lipoprotein transport | intervention: LPL loss-of-function (OMIM 238600): do(LPL activity down) -> plasma lipoprotein particle concentration up
causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.mechanism: LPL activity drives lipolytic clearance of TG-rich lipoprotein particles from the circulation; without LPL activity, chylomicrons and VLDL accumulate, raising total plasma lipoprotein particle number.

causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.evidence: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism; OMIM 238600 (LPL deficiency / familial chylomicronemia syndrome); Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology, lipoprotein transport | intervention: LPL loss-of-function (familial chylomicronemia syndrome): do(LPL activity down) -> total plasma lipids up
causal:influence:lipoprotein_lipase_acti.mechanism: LPL hydrolyses core triacylglycerol of TG-rich lipoprotein particles (chylomicrons, VLDL), driving their clearance; LPL loss-of-function (familial chylomicronemia syndrome, OMIM 238600) causes massive hypertriglyceridaemia and elevated total plasma lipids due to failure to clear TG-rich particles.

causal:influence:lung_elastic_recoil_pre.evidence: "The FEV1.0 ... is reduced by an increase in airway resistance or a reduction in elastic recoil of the lung"; "flow is limited by airway compression and is determined by the elastic recoil force of the lung and the resistance of the airways upstream of the collapse point" (West's Respiratory Physiology, 11th ed., ch 10)
causal:influence:lung_elastic_recoil_pre.mechanism: during dynamic compression the flow-limited expiratory flow (FEV1.0) is set by the lung elastic recoil pressure driving gas through airways upstream of the collapse point; reduced recoil lowers FEV1.0

causal:influence:macula_densa_nacl_signa.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (macula-densa tubuloglomerular feedback and afferent arteriolar control of GFR).
causal:influence:macula_densa_nacl_signa.mechanism: increased macula-densa NaCl delivery activates tubuloglomerular feedback, causing afferent arteriolar vasoconstriction and lowering GFR

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases; GeneReviews MCAD deficiency (ACADM, OMIM 201450): elevated free medium-chain fatty acids including hexanoic acid (C6) in urine organic-acid profiles; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 17 | intervention: MCAD deficiency (ACADM loss-of-function, OMIM 201450)
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: MCAD oxidises hexanoyl-CoA (C6); deficiency backs up C6 acyl-CoA, hydrolysed to free hexanoic acid which is excreted — reduced MCAD activity raises urinary hexanoic acid

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: MCAD deficiency (ACADM, OMIM 201450); Rinaldo et al., GeneReviews NBK1424: elevated dicarboxylic acids (adipic C6, suberic C8, sebacic C10) are hallmarks of MCAD deficiency; Chalmers et al., JIMD 1985 (PMID 6434844): GC-MS diagnosis of MCAD deficiency showing elevated suberic acid | intervention: genetic LoF of ACADM gene (biallelic mutation; autosomal recessive MCAD deficiency) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: MCAD deficiency blocks beta-oxidation of medium-chain fatty acids; unoxidised C8 (octanoate) and C10 (decanoate) fatty acids undergo omega-oxidation to dicarboxylic acids, yielding suberic acid (octanedioic acid, C8-DC) as a major product — reduced MCAD activity raises urinary suberic acid

causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.evidence: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-5.2 (5.2: Passive Transport): 'One of the effects of high blood pressure is the appearance of protein in the urine, which abnormally high pressure squeezes through.'
causal:influence:mean_arterial_pressure:.mechanism: Elevated blood pressure increases the hydrostatic pressure across the glomerular filtration barrier, forcing protein that would normally be retained into the renal tubular filtrate and thence into urine.

causal:influence:metabolic_rate:positive.evidence: Physiological Reviews 2014 (PMID thyroid hormone regulation of metabolism: T3 is the principal determinant of BMR; BMR ≡ REE under standardised resting conditions); Frontiers in Physiology 2026 (associations between resting and total energy expenditure and thyroid hormone levels — REE tracks metabolic_rate). | intervention: hyperthyroidism raises metabolic_rate and REE; hypothyroidism lowers both; beta-adrenergic stimulation (epinephrine) raises REE acutely
causal:influence:metabolic_rate:positive.mechanism: Resting energy expenditure (REE) is the principal operational measurement of basal/resting metabolic rate (BMR/RMR): both measure the rate of energy consumption at rest (O2 uptake / heat generation). Thyroid hormone, sympathetic tone, lean mass, and temperature set metabolic_rate; changes in metabolic_rate are reflected 1:1 in resting energy expenditure.

causal:influence:methylmalonyl_coa_mutas.evidence: GeneReviews NBK1231 (Isolated Methylmalonic Acidemia: lactic acidemia is a defining metabolic crisis feature); PMC10715492 (New insights into MMA pathophysiology: methylmalonic acid inhibits respiratory chain; secondary lactic acidosis); OMIM 251000 (methylmalonic acidemia, MMUT type: lactate, ammonia elevated in acute decompensation). | intervention: do(MMUT LoF) — biallelic MMUT mutations causing methylmalonic acidemia (OMIM 251000) | intervention: do(MMUT loss-of-function) — biallelic mutations in MMUT gene causing isolated methylmalonic acidemia (OMIM 251000)
causal:influence:methylmalonyl_coa_mutas.mechanism: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (MMUT) converts methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA for TCA-cycle entry. MMUT deficiency (methylmalonic acidemia, MMA) causes accumulation of methylmalonic acid and 2-methylcitric acid, which inhibit the mitochondrial respiratory chain (complex I/II) and reduce aerobic oxidation flux; anaerobic glycolysis is upregulated, increasing pyruvate-to-lactate conversion. The resulting lactic acidosis is a hallmark metabolic crisis in MMA. do(MMUT activity down) → plasma_lactate up; do(MMUT activity up) → plasma_lactate down.

causal:influence:motor_unit_recruitment:.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-056 (10.5: Nervous System Control of Muscle Tension): 'As more motor units are recruited, the muscle contraction grows progressively stronger'; 'the largest motor units may generate a contractile force of 50 times more than the smallest motor units in the muscle'
causal:influence:motor_unit_recruitment:.mechanism: Activating more motor units (each comprising a motor neuron and its innervated muscle fibers) adds their contractile forces; larger motor units contribute disproportionately more force (up to 50x that of smallest units)

causal:influence:muscle_glycogen_synthas.evidence: Glycogen storage disease type 0b (muscle), OMIM:611556 — GYS1 LoF causes severe muscle glycogen deficiency; patients present with exercise intolerance and fasting hypoglycemia due to absent muscle glycogen stores
causal:influence:muscle_glycogen_synthas.mechanism: RHEA:18549 (EC 2.4.1.11): [(1->4)-alpha-D-glucosyl](n) + UDP-alpha-D-glucose = [(1->4)-alpha-D-glucosyl](n+1) + UDP + H(+); muscle glycogen is the direct polymer product of GYS1 elongation

causal:influence:nuclear_srebp2_activity.evidence: INTERVENTIONAL. PCSK9 gain-of-function -> autosomal-dominant hypercholesterolemia; PCSK9 loss-of-function -> low LDL (genetic do()); statin-driven SREBP-2 activation co-induces PCSK9 (the rationale for combining statins with PCSK9 inhibitors). DRAFT for domain review.
causal:influence:nuclear_srebp2_activity.mechanism: PCSK9 is a direct SREBP-2 transcriptional target (quality: nuclear SREBP-2 activity -> disposition: SRE occupancy at the PCSK9 promoter -> process: PCSK9 transcription -> quality: PCSK9 concentration)

causal:influence:osteoblast_activity:pos.evidence: "When the remodeling process is uncoupled so that resorption exceeds formation, bone is lost. However, during peak bone acquisition, formation exceeds resorption, resulting in a net gain of bone." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 30, p 1267
causal:influence:osteoblast_activity:pos.mechanism: Osteoblasts synthesize collagen and mineralize bone matrix, increasing skeletal mass

causal:influence:osteocyte_sclerostin:ne.evidence: Li 2005 J Biol Chem PMID:15778503 [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:osteocyte_sclerostin:ne.mechanism: Sclerostin (SOST) binds LRP5/6 co-receptor and antagonizes canonical Wnt signaling in osteoblasts -> reduced bone formation (GO:0030279 negative regulation of ossification)

causal:influence:oxygen_delivery:negativ.evidence: If, for example, O2 delivery declines, while tissue O2 utilization remains constant, oxygen extraction from the blood must increase to meet the metabolic needs
causal:influence:oxygen_delivery:negativ.mechanism: when O2 delivery falls at constant tissue utilization, O2 extraction from blood must rise to meet metabolic needs

causal:influence:pdh_complex_activity:ne.evidence: PDH deficiency (OMIM 312170): Stacpoole (1986) Metabolism 35:830-843 (lactic acidosis in PDH deficiency); Robinson (2006) Mitochondrion 6:257-263 (PDH deficiency and lactic acidosis); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (pyruvate dehydrogenase reaction and lactic acidosis in PDH deficiency). Intervention: do(PDH complex LoF). | intervention: genetic loss-of-function of PDH complex (PDH deficiency, OMIM 312170) causing lactic acidosis
causal:influence:pdh_complex_activity:ne.mechanism: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (PDH) irreversibly converts pyruvate to acetyl-CoA; when PDH activity is reduced, pyruvate that cannot enter the TCA cycle is instead reduced to lactate by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH). PDH deficiency (PDHA1 or PDHB mutations, OMIM 312170) causes lactic acidosis — elevated plasma and CSF lactate — because the pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA flux is impaired and lactate accumulates. Active PDH reduces plasma lactate by clearing pyruvate into the TCA cycle.

causal:influence:phosphomannomutase_acti.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (N-glycosylation pathway: mannose-1-P → GDP-mannose is required for dolichol-PP-oligosaccharide assembly); Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray Inborn Metabolic Diseases (PMM2-CDG, CDG-Ia, OMIM 212065: most common CDG — serum transferrin isoelectrofocusing shows type I CDG pattern, reduced normally glycosylated tetrasialo-transferrin); Harrison's Principles (CDG syndromes — PMM2 deficiency). | intervention: PMM2 loss-of-function (PMM2-CDG, OMIM 212065): do(phosphomannomutase_activity↓) → GDP-mannose↓ → hypoglycosylation of serotransferrin → plasma_transferrin_glycoform_ratio↓
causal:influence:phosphomannomutase_acti.mechanism: PMM2 converts mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate, which is the precursor for GDP-mannose synthesis. GDP-mannose is the essential sugar nucleotide donor for mannose incorporation into N-linked glycans in the ER. PMM2 LoF (PMM2-CDG / CDG-Ia, OMIM 212065) → GDP-mannose deficiency → incomplete N-glycosylation of secreted glycoproteins including serotransferrin → CDG type-I transferrin isoelectrofocusing pattern (elevated disialo- and asialo-transferrin) → proportion of correctly glycosylated transferrin (tetrasialo-form) falls. PMM2 activity ↑ → adequate GDP-mannose → complete N-glycosylation → normal transferrin glycoform ratio ↑.

causal:influence:phosphomannose_isomeras.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray Inborn Metabolic Diseases (MPI-CDG / CDG-Ib, OMIM 602579: type I CDG transferrin pattern; oral mannose supplementation corrects glycosylation by bypassing MPI — confirms the flux control); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (mannose-6-phosphate in N-glycan biosynthesis pathway); Harrison's Principles (CDG-Ib: treatable CDG with mannose supplementation). | intervention: MPI loss-of-function (MPI-CDG / CDG-Ib, OMIM 602579): do(phosphomannose_isomerase_activity↓) → mannose-6-P↓ → GDP-mannose↓ → transferrin hypoglycosylation → plasma_transferrin_glycoform_ratio↓
causal:influence:phosphomannose_isomeras.mechanism: MPI (phosphomannose isomerase / mannose-6-phosphate isomerase) interconverts fructose-6-phosphate ↔ mannose-6-phosphate, providing mannose-6-P for the GDP-mannose synthetic pathway. MPI LoF (MPI-CDG / CDG-Ib, OMIM 602579) → mannose-6-P deficiency → GDP-mannose deficiency → N-glycosylation defect → CDG type-I transferrin isoelectrofocusing pattern (reduced normally glycosylated tetrasialo-transferrin). MPI activity ↑ → mannose-6-P maintained → GDP-mannose adequate → complete glycosylation → normal transferrin glycoform ratio ↑.

causal:influence:pituitary_fsh_secretion.evidence: BioModels BIOMD0000000494 (Roblitz2013) models plasma FSH as the gonadotroph secretory output into the circulation. Curated by Paul N. Schofield. *** DRAFT FOR REVIEW ***
causal:influence:pituitary_fsh_secretion.mechanism: anterior-pituitary gonadotroph FSH secretory output sets the circulating FSH concentration (mass balance: plasma [FSH] = secretion − clearance)

Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 8, p. 205

causal:influence:pituitary_gh:positive:m.evidence: Moller & Jorgensen 2009, Endocr Rev 30(2):152-77 (PMID 19240267) — GH activates hormone-sensitive lipase, raising lipolysis, FFA oxidation and resting energy expenditure [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:pituitary_gh:positive:m.mechanism: GH stimulates lipolysis and increases whole-body energy expenditure / oxygen consumption.

causal:influence:pituitary_prolactin_sec.mechanism: anterior-pituitary lactotroph PRL secretory output sets the circulating prolactin concentration (mass balance: plasma [PRL] = secretion − clearance)

causal:influence:plasma_17ohp:positive:p.evidence: SIGNOR-268650 (mechanism: precursor of) | PMID:17192295 resolved (J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2007, P450c17 deficiency) — concordant: describes dual 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase activity of CYP17A1; deficiency abolishes both reactions, confirming 17OHP is the precursor for androstenedione via this enzyme | *** DRAFT FOR REVIEW (imported) ***
causal:influence:plasma_17ohp:positive:p.mechanism: CYP17A1 17,20-lyase cleaves the C17-C20 bond of 17alpha-hydroxyprogesterone to yield androstenedione; more substrate raises product (enzyme kinetics, normal adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis)

causal:influence:plasma_5_methyltetrahyd.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (folate coenzymes in one-carbon metabolism and thymidylate synthesis); Harrison's 'Folate deficiency and megaloblastic anemia'; GeneReviews FOLR1 / OMIM 613068 (cerebral folate transport deficiency); Lucock M Mol Genet Metab 2000 (folate-dependent thymidylate synthesis in proliferating cells). | intervention: do(plasma folate / 5-MTHF deficiency, as in dietary folate deficiency or FOLR1 LoF)
causal:influence:plasma_5_methyltetrahyd.mechanism: 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF) is both the circulating folate form and the methyl donor for homocysteine remethylation (via methionine synthase). Folate deficiency — or FOLR1-mediated cerebral folate transport deficiency causing isolated CSF/tissue folate depletion — depletes the THF pool required for de novo thymidylate synthesis (thymidylate synthase) and purine synthesis. Erythroblasts depend on this for DNA replication; deficiency produces megaloblastic bone-marrow changes and impaired erythroblast proliferation. do(plasma 5-MTHF deficiency) → erythroblast proliferation decreases.

causal:influence:plasma_arachidonic_acid.evidence: PMID 24184513; (Abstract (Identification of genes and pathways involved in the synthesis of Mead acid (20:3n-9), an indicator of essential fatty acid deficiency)); “Mead acid (20:3n-9) is synthesized from oleic acid during a state of essential fatty acid deficiency (EFAD).” | When essential fatty acids (the arachidonic-acid supply) are low, Mead acid synthesis turns on, i.e. do(lower arachidonic) increases Mead acid. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:plasma_arachidonic_acid.mechanism: low arachidonic acid (essential-fatty-acid deficiency) de-represses the shared delta-6/delta-5 desaturase-elongase, which instead elongates/desaturates oleic acid to Mead acid -> Mead acid rises (basis of the Holman triene:tetraene ratio)

causal:influence:plasma_calcitonin:negat.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-034 (Exercise, Nutrition, Hormones, and Bone Tissue): 'Calcitonin inhibits osteoclast activity and stimulates calcium uptake by the bones, thus reducing the concentration of calcium ions in the blood.' | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-37.3 (37.3: Regulation of Body Processes): 'Calcitonin decreases blood calcium levels by inhibiting osteoclasts, stimulating osteoblasts, and stimulating calcium excretion by the kidneys.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-37.5 (37.5: Endocrine Glands): 'The combination of these two events [inhibit osteoclast activity; stimulate renal calcium excretion] lowers body fluid levels of calcium.'
causal:influence:plasma_calcitonin:negat.mechanism: Calcitonin stimulates calcium uptake by bones and inhibits osteoclasts, thereby lowering plasma calcium concentration

causal:influence:plasma_calcium:positive.evidence: StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf), Physiology, Calcium; (Physiology, Calcium, NBK482128); “Calcitonin is released by the thyroid parafollicular cells (C-cells) in response to an increase in serum calcium.” | Elevated serum calcium stimulates C-cell calcitonin release, supporting do(plasma calcium up) -> calcitonin secretion up (+).
causal:influence:plasma_calcium:positive.mechanism: elevated extracellular ionised Ca2+ activates the CaSR on thyroid parafollicular C cells -> Gq/PLC -> increased calcitonin secretion

causal:influence:plasma_cck:positive:fec.evidence: Mechanism: CCK is the dominant acinar enzyme-secretagogue; fecal elastase-1 is a stable, pancreas-specific marker of acinar secretory/functional capacity that falls in exocrine pancreatic insufficiency and rises with secretory output. CITATION (verified): Walkowiak J et al., 'Fecal elastase-1 concentration: an indirect test of exocrine pancreatic function and a marker of an enteropathy regardless of cause', PMID:12604968 (title/PMID confirmed via PubMed). Textbook anchor: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed., Ch. 64 (pancreatic secretion regulated by CCK and secretin).
